issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Farm to provide a no-argument constructor that initializes the ArrayList (and template Main instantiates Farm with new Farm()). However, the solution's Farm class only defines a constructor Farm(int initialCapacity) and does not provide a no-arg constructor. This constructor parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent code that uses new Farm() (as shown in the template Main and required by the specification) from compiling against the solution's Farm implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) so the class matches the problem specification and the template usage (or alternatively, provide both the existing Farm(int) and a no-arg Farm()).
